grades.quote: 2.3.1. Reserved Writes Preserve Values, Reads Ignore Values (WPRI)
grades.reason: The table of contents only expands the WPRI, WLRL and WARL acronyms through section titles. It gives no read/write guarantees or software obligations.

grades.quote: Software should ignore the values read from these fields, and should preserve the values held in these fields when writing values to other fields of the same register. For forward compatibility, implementations that do not furnish these fields must make them read-only zero.
grades.reason: It fully defines WPRI: software ignores values read, preserves values on writes to other fields, and unimplemented fields are read-only zero. It does not cover WLRL or WARL, so it answers only part of the query.

grades.quote: Each `xenvcfg` register is WARL; however, software should determine the legal values from the execution environment discovery mechanism.
grades.reason: It gives one example of WARL use (xenvcfg registers) and says software must discover the legal values. It does not define WARL, WPRI or WLRL.
It is only a section heading and a one-sentence intro. It defines none of WPRI, WLRL or WARL.
